              f"{fmt(A * nsq / log2(n))}  {fmt(R * nsq if R is not None else None)}  "
              f"{float(X / g):>10.5f}  {float(A / X):>10.5f}")
    print(f"{'limit':>8}  {fmt(CAP_CONST)}  {fmt(GAP_CONST)}  {fmt(Decimal(1))}  "
          f"{fmt(CAP_CONST)}  {float(RATIO_CONST):>10.5f}  {'inf':>10}")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 2 — the exact constants and the refuted guess
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_constants(n_big: int = 655360) -> None:
    rule("2. The exact constants (and the refutation of X/g -> 2)")
    n = Decimal(n_big)
    nsq = n * n
    X, A, g = capacity_channel(n), ambiguity_channel(n), gap_channel(n)
    R = reverse_channel(n)
    assert R is not None
    Is = A + R

    rows: List[Tuple[str, Decimal, Decimal]] = [
        ("g * n^2        -> log2 e - 1", g * nsq, GAP_CONST),
        ("X * n^2        -> 2 log2 e  ", X * nsq, CAP_CONST),
        ("A * n^2/log2 n == 1         ", A * nsq / log2(n), Decimal(1)),
        ("(Is - A) * n^2 -> 2 log2 e  ", (Is - A) * nsq, CAP_CONST),
        ("X / g          -> 2/(1-ln2) ", X / g, RATIO_CONST),
    ]
    print(f"evaluated at n = {n_big} with {getcontext().prec}-digit arithmetic\n")
    print(f"{'law':<30}  {'computed':>20}  {'constant':>20}  {'|deviation|':>12}")
    for name, computed, target in rows:

    print(f"pre-data guess  X/g -> 2          : deviation "

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 3 — the proved finite-n rate bounds
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_rates(ns: List[int]) -> None:
    rule("3. Proved finite-n error bounds versus observed errors")
    print(f"{'n':>8}  {'|g n^2 - c_g|':>14} {'bound 1/(n ln2)':>16} "
          f"{'|X n^2 - c_X|':>14} {'bound 24/(n ln2)':>17} "
          f"{'|R n^2 - c_X|':>14} {'bound 16/(n ln2)':>17}")
    for k in ns:
        n = Decimal(k)
        nsq = n * n
        eg = abs(gap_channel(n) * nsq - GAP_CONST)
        eX = abs(capacity_channel(n) * nsq - CAP_CONST)
        R = reverse_channel(n)
        eR = abs(R * nsq - CAP_CONST) if R is not None else None
        bg, bX, bR = 1 / (n * LN2), 24 / (n * LN2), 16 / (n * LN2)
        ok = (eg <= bg) and (eX <= bX or k < 4) and (eR is None or eR <= bR or k < 4)
        print(f"{k:>8}  {float(eg):>14.3e} {float(bg):>16.3e} "

              f"{(float(eR) if eR is not None else float('inf')):>14.3e} "

    print("\n(The bounds are deliberately crude: the true errors are O(1/n^2),")
    print(" because the underlying fork function F(x) = (1+x)ln(1+x)+(1-x)ln(1-x) is even.)")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 4 — collapse at n = 2
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_collapse() -> None:
    rule("4. The collapse point n = 2")
    two = Decimal(2)
    X2, A2, g2 = capacity_channel(two), ambiguity_channel(two), gap_channel(two)
    g2_exact = Decimal(5) / 4 - (Decimal(3) / 4) * log2(Decimal(3))
    print(f"  X(2) = {float(X2):.12f}   (exact value 1: the coin is a certainty, H(1) = 0)")
    print(f"  A(2) = {float(A2):.12f}   (exact value 1/4)")
    print(f"  g(2) = {float(g2):.12f}   (exact value 5/4 - (3/4) log2 3 = "
          f"{float(g2_exact):.12f})")
    print(f"  g(2) * 4 = {float(g2 * 4):.12f}   (matches the tabulated g*n^2 at n = 2)")
    print(f"  R(2) : {reverse_channel(two)}   -- diverges: 1 - 4/n^2 = 0 at n = 2")
    print(f"  Is(2): {isolation_channel(two)}   -- diverges for the same reason")
    print()
    print("  Note: the forward divergence from a certainty to a fair coin is one bit,")
    print("  but the reverse divergence is infinite, since the fair coin gives positive")
    print("  probability to an event the certainty declares impossible.")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 5 — the A/X crossing in (7,8) with integer certificates
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_crossing() -> None:
    rule("5. The A/X sign flip lies exactly in the window (7, 8)")
    for k in range(2, 13):
        n = Decimal(k)
        A, X = ambiguity_channel(n), capacity_channel(n)
        mark = "A < X" if A < X else "A > X"
        print(f"  n = {k:>2}:  A = {float(A):.9f}   X = {float(X):.9f}   "

    lhs7, rhs7 = 7 ** 100, 3 ** 126 * 5 ** 35
    lhs8, rhs8 = 5 ** 40 * 3 ** 24, 2 ** 131
    print(f"    A(7) < X(7)  <=>  7^100 < 3^126 * 5^35")
    print(f"        7^100        = {lhs7}")
    print(f"        3^126 * 5^35 = {rhs7}")
    print(f"        holds: {lhs7 < rhs7}")
    print(f"    X(8) < A(8)  <=>  5^40 * 3^24 < 2^131")
    print(f"        5^40 * 3^24  = {lhs8}")
    print(f"        2^131        = {rhs8}")
    print(f"        holds: {lhs8 < rhs8}")

    lo, hi = Decimal(7), Decimal(8)
    f: Callable[[Decimal], Decimal] = lambda t: ambiguity_channel(t) - capacity_channel(t)
    for _ in range(80):
        mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        if f(lo) * f(mid) <= 0:
            hi = mid
        else:
            lo = mid
    print(f"\n  Real crossing point n* = {float((lo + hi) / 2):.12f}  (bisection in (7,8))")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 6 — the closed form X(n) = F(2/n)/(2 ln 2) and its cubic window
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_fork_identity(ns: List[int]) -> None:
    rule("6. The closed form X(n) = F(2/n)/(2 ln 2) and the cubic window |F(x)-x^2| <= 6|x|^3")
    print(f"{'n':>8}  {'X(n)':>18}  {'F(2/n)/(2 ln2)':>18}  {'|difference|':>13}"
          f"  {'|F(x)-x^2|':>12}  {'6|x|^3':>12}")
    for k in ns:
        n = Decimal(k)
        x = Decimal(2) / n
        lhs = capacity_channel(n)
        rhs = fork_function(x) / (2 * LN2)
        err = abs(fork_function(x) - x * x)
        bnd = 6 * abs(x) ** 3
        print(f"{k:>8}  {float(lhs):>18.14f}  {float(rhs):>18.14f}  "
              f"{float(abs(lhs - rhs)):>13.3e}  {float(err):>12.3e}  {float(bnd):>12.3e}")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main() -> None:
    print(__doc__)
    demo_table([2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 16, 17, 100, 1000, 100000, 655360])
    demo_constants(655360)
    demo_rates([2, 4, 8, 16, 100, 1000, 100000, 655360])
    demo_collapse()
    demo_crossing()
    demo_fork_identity([4, 8, 16, 100, 1000, 100000])
    rule("All demonstrated laws agree with the proved statements.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def capacity_channel(n: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    """X(n) = 1 - H(1/2 + 1/n): bits lost relative to a fair coin."""
    return Decimal(1) - binary_entropy(Decimal(1) / 2 + Decimal(1) / n)


def ambiguity_channel(n: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    """A(n) = log2 n / n^2."""
    return log2(n) / (n * n)


def gap_channel(n: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    """g(n) = -(1 - 1/n^2) log2(1 - 1/n^2) - 1/n^2."""
    u = Decimal(1) / (n * n)
    return -(Decimal(1) - u) * log2(Decimal(1) - u) - u


def reverse_channel(n: Decimal) -> Optional[Decimal]:
    """R(n) = -(1/2) log2(1 - 4/n^2); undefined (infinite) at n = 2."""
    v = Decimal(4) / (n * n)
    if v >= 1:
        return None
    return -(Decimal(1) / 2) * log2(Decimal(1) - v)


def isolation_channel(n: Decimal) -> Optional[Decimal]:
    """Is(n) = A(n) + R(n)."""
    r = reverse_channel(n)
    return None if r is None else ambiguity_channel(n) + r


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The fork function, and the closed form X(n) = F(2/n) / (2 ln 2)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def fork_function(x: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    """F(x) = (1+x) ln(1+x) + (1-x) ln(1-x); even, non-negative, F(x) = x^2 + O(x^4)."""
    return (1 + x) * (1 + x).ln() + (1 - x) * (1 - x).ln()


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reporting helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def fmt(x: Optional[Decimal], digits: int = 9) -> str:
    if x is None:
        return "        inf"
    return f"{float(x):>{digits + 4}.{digits}f}"


def rule(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)

def demo_constants(n_big: int = 655360) -> None:
    rule("2. The exact constants (and the refutation of X/g -> 2)")
    n = Decimal(n_big)
    nsq = n * n
    X, A, g = capacity_channel(n), ambiguity_channel(n), gap_channel(n)
    R = reverse_channel(n)
    assert R is not None
    Is = A + R

    rows: List[Tuple[str, Decimal, Decimal]] = [
        ("g * n^2        -> log2 e - 1", g * nsq, GAP_CONST),
        ("X * n^2        -> 2 log2 e  ", X * nsq, CAP_CONST),
        ("A * n^2/log2 n == 1         ", A * nsq / log2(n), Decimal(1)),
        ("(Is - A) * n^2 -> 2 log2 e  ", (Is - A) * nsq, CAP_CONST),
        ("X / g          -> 2/(1-ln2) ", X / g, RATIO_CONST),
    ]
    print(f"evaluated at n = {n_big} with {getcontext().prec}-digit arithmetic\n")
    print(f"{'law':<30}  {'computed':>20}  {'constant':>20}  {'|deviation|':>12}")
    for name, computed, target in rows:
        dev = abs(computed - target)
        print(f"{name:<30}  {float(computed):>20.12f}  {float(target):>20.12f}"
              f"  {float(dev):>12.3e}")

    print()
    print(f"pre-data guess  X/g -> 2          : deviation "
          f"{float(abs(X / g - 2)):.6f}   REFUTED")
    print(f"corrected law   X/g -> 2/(1-ln 2) : deviation "
          f"{float(abs(X / g - RATIO_CONST)):.3e}   confirmed")
    print()
    print("Why 6.5178 and not 2 — the near-cancellation inside g:")
    print(f"  entropy term alone contributes  log2 e     = {float(LOG2E):.6f}")
    print(f"  the definition subtracts        1          = 1.000000")
    print(f"  leaving                         log2 e - 1 = {float(GAP_CONST):.6f}")
    print(f"  so the ratio is inflated by 1/(1-ln 2)     = "
          f"{float(1 / (1 - LN2)):.6f}  (2 x this = {float(RATIO_CONST):.6f})")

def demo_rates(ns: List[int]) -> None:
    rule("3. Proved finite-n error bounds versus observed errors")
    print(f"{'n':>8}  {'|g n^2 - c_g|':>14} {'bound 1/(n ln2)':>16} "
          f"{'|X n^2 - c_X|':>14} {'bound 24/(n ln2)':>17} "
          f"{'|R n^2 - c_X|':>14} {'bound 16/(n ln2)':>17}")
    for k in ns:
        n = Decimal(k)
        nsq = n * n
        eg = abs(gap_channel(n) * nsq - GAP_CONST)
        eX = abs(capacity_channel(n) * nsq - CAP_CONST)
        R = reverse_channel(n)
        eR = abs(R * nsq - CAP_CONST) if R is not None else None
        bg, bX, bR = 1 / (n * LN2), 24 / (n * LN2), 16 / (n * LN2)
        ok = (eg <= bg) and (eX <= bX or k < 4) and (eR is None or eR <= bR or k < 4)
        print(f"{k:>8}  {float(eg):>14.3e} {float(bg):>16.3e} "
              f"{float(eX):>14.3e} {float(bX):>17.3e} "
              f"{(float(eR) if eR is not None else float('inf')):>14.3e} "
              f"{float(bR):>17.3e}   {'ok' if ok else '!!'}")
    print("\n(The bounds are deliberately crude: the true errors are O(1/n^2),")
    print(" because the underlying fork function F(x) = (1+x)ln(1+x)+(1-x)ln(1-x) is even.)")

def demo_collapse() -> None:
    rule("4. The collapse point n = 2")
    two = Decimal(2)
    X2, A2, g2 = capacity_channel(two), ambiguity_channel(two), gap_channel(two)
    g2_exact = Decimal(5) / 4 - (Decimal(3) / 4) * log2(Decimal(3))
    print(f"  X(2) = {float(X2):.12f}   (exact value 1: the coin is a certainty, H(1) = 0)")
    print(f"  A(2) = {float(A2):.12f}   (exact value 1/4)")
    print(f"  g(2) = {float(g2):.12f}   (exact value 5/4 - (3/4) log2 3 = "
          f"{float(g2_exact):.12f})")
    print(f"  g(2) * 4 = {float(g2 * 4):.12f}   (matches the tabulated g*n^2 at n = 2)")
    print(f"  R(2) : {reverse_channel(two)}   -- diverges: 1 - 4/n^2 = 0 at n = 2")
    print(f"  Is(2): {isolation_channel(two)}   -- diverges for the same reason")
    print()
    print("  Note: the forward divergence from a certainty to a fair coin is one bit,")
    print("  but the reverse divergence is infinite, since the fair coin gives positive")
    print("  probability to an event the certainty declares impossible.")

def demo_crossing() -> None:
    rule("5. The A/X sign flip lies exactly in the window (7, 8)")
    for k in range(2, 13):
        n = Decimal(k)
        A, X = ambiguity_channel(n), capacity_channel(n)
        mark = "A < X" if A < X else "A > X"
        print(f"  n = {k:>2}:  A = {float(A):.9f}   X = {float(X):.9f}   "
              f"A/X = {float(A / X):.6f}   {mark}")

    print("\n  Integer certificates (exact arithmetic, no floating point):")
    lhs7, rhs7 = 7 ** 100, 3 ** 126 * 5 ** 35
    lhs8, rhs8 = 5 ** 40 * 3 ** 24, 2 ** 131
    print(f"    A(7) < X(7)  <=>  7^100 < 3^126 * 5^35")
    print(f"        7^100        = {lhs7}")
    print(f"        3^126 * 5^35 = {rhs7}")
    print(f"        holds: {lhs7 < rhs7}")
    print(f"    X(8) < A(8)  <=>  5^40 * 3^24 < 2^131")
    print(f"        5^40 * 3^24  = {lhs8}")
    print(f"        2^131        = {rhs8}")
    print(f"        holds: {lhs8 < rhs8}")

    # Locate the real crossing point by bisection on A - X.
    lo, hi = Decimal(7), Decimal(8)
    f: Callable[[Decimal], Decimal] = lambda t: ambiguity_channel(t) - capacity_channel(t)
    for _ in range(80):
        mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        if f(lo) * f(mid) <= 0:
            hi = mid
        else:
            lo = mid
    print(f"\n  Real crossing point n* = {float((lo + hi) / 2):.12f}  (bisection in (7,8))")

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_fork_identity(ns: List[int]) -> None:
    rule("6. The closed form X(n) = F(2/n)/(2 ln 2) and the cubic window |F(x)-x^2| <= 6|x|^3")
    print(f"{'n':>8}  {'X(n)':>18}  {'F(2/n)/(2 ln2)':>18}  {'|difference|':>13}"
          f"  {'|F(x)-x^2|':>12}  {'6|x|^3':>12}")
    for k in ns:
        n = Decimal(k)
        x = Decimal(2) / n
        lhs = capacity_channel(n)
        rhs = fork_function(x) / (2 * LN2)
        err = abs(fork_function(x) - x * x)

        print(f"{k:>8}  {float(lhs):>18.14f}  {float(rhs):>18.14f}  "
              f"{float(abs(lhs - rhs)):>13.3e}  {float(err):>12.3e}  {float(bnd):>12.3e}")

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from decimal import Decimal, getcontext
from typing import Dict, List, Optional


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ChannelRow:
    """All channel data at one resolution, with the certification verdicts."""
    n: int
    X: Decimal
    A: Decimal
    g: Decimal
    R: Optional[Decimal]
    X_scaled: Decimal            # X n^2
    A_scaled: Decimal            # A n^2 / log2 n  (identically 1)
    g_scaled: Decimal            # g n^2
    R_scaled: Optional[Decimal]  # R n^2
    ratio_Xg: Decimal            # X / g
    ratio_AX: Decimal            # A / X
    bounds_ok: Dict[str, bool]   # proved-rate certification verdicts


def fork_channel_row(n: int, precision: int = 50) -> ChannelRow:
    """Evaluate all four channels at resolution n and certify the proved rate bounds."""
    if n < 2:
        raise ValueError("resolution n must be at least 2")
    getcontext().prec = precision + 10

    ln2: Decimal = Decimal(2).ln()
    log2e: Decimal = Decimal(1) / ln2
    gap_const: Decimal = log2e - 1
    cap_const: Decimal = 2 * log2e

    def log2(x: Decimal) -> Decimal:
        return x.ln() / ln2

    N = Decimal(n)
    nsq = N * N

    # capacity channel X(n) = 1 - H(1/2 + 1/n)
    p = Decimal(1) / 2 + Decimal(1) / N
    q = Decimal(1) - p
    ent = (Decimal(0) if p == 0 else -p * log2(p)) + \
          (Decimal(0) if q == 0 else -q * log2(q))
    X = Decimal(1) - ent

    # ambiguity channel
    A = log2(N) / nsq

    # gap channel
    u = Decimal(1) / nsq
    g = -(Decimal(1) - u) * log2(Decimal(1) - u) - u

    # reverse channel (undefined at n = 2)
    v = Decimal(4) / nsq
    R: Optional[Decimal] = None if v >= 1 else -(Decimal(1) / 2) * log2(Decimal(1) - v)

    verdicts: Dict[str, bool] = {
        "gap rate |g n^2 - (log2 e - 1)| <= 1/(n ln2)":
            abs(g * nsq - gap_const) <= 1 / (N * ln2),
        "capacity rate |X n^2 - 2 log2 e| <= 24/(n ln2)":
            n < 4 or abs(X * nsq - cap_const) <= 24 / (N * ln2),
        "reverse rate |R n^2 - 2 log2 e| <= 16/(n ln2)":
            R is None or n < 4 or abs(R * nsq - cap_const) <= 16 / (N * ln2),
        "ambiguity identity A n^2 / log2 n == 1":
            abs(A * nsq / log2(N) - 1) < Decimal(10) ** (-(precision - 2)),
    }

    return ChannelRow(
        n=n, X=X, A=A, g=g, R=R,
        X_scaled=X * nsq,
        A_scaled=A * nsq / log2(N),
        g_scaled=g * nsq,
        R_scaled=None if R is None else R * nsq,
        ratio_Xg=X / g,
        ratio_AX=A / X,
        bounds_ok=verdicts,
    )


def fork_channel_table(resolutions: List[int], precision: int = 50) -> List[ChannelRow]:
    """Evaluate and certify the channels at a list of resolutions."""
    return [fork_channel_row(n, precision) for n in resolutions]

from __future__ import annotations

from fractions import Fraction
from math import gcd
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

LogCombo = Dict[int, Fraction]   # base -> rational coefficient, meaning sum c * ln(base)


def combo_sub(lhs: LogCombo, rhs: LogCombo) -> LogCombo:
    """Return lhs - rhs as a single logarithmic combination."""
    out: LogCombo = dict(lhs)
    for base, coeff in rhs.items():
        out[base] = out.get(base, Fraction(0)) - coeff
    return {b: c for b, c in out.items() if c != 0}


def integer_certificate(lhs: LogCombo, rhs: LogCombo) -> Tuple[int, int, bool, int]:
    """
    Decide  sum lhs  <  sum rhs  exactly.

    Returns (L, R, verdict, D) where D is the common denominator used and
    L = prod base^(D*coeff) over positive net coefficients, R likewise for negatives,
    so that the original inequality is equivalent to L < R.
    """
    diff = combo_sub(lhs, rhs)                      # want: sum diff < 0
    denom = 1
    for c in diff.values():
        denom = denom * c.denominator // gcd(denom, c.denominator)
    left, right = 1, 1
    for base, coeff in diff.items():
        e = int(coeff * denom)
        if e > 0:
            left *= base ** e
        else:
            right *= base ** (-e)
    return left, right, left < right, denom


def capacity_combo(n: int) -> Tuple[LogCombo, Fraction]:

    Return (C, s) such that X(n) = (sum over C of c*ln(base)) / (s * ln 2).

    Uses X(n) = F(2/n)/(2 ln 2) with F(x) = (1+x)ln(1+x) + (1-x)ln(1-x); the two
    arguments 1 +- 2/n are rationals, and their logarithms expand over the prime
    factorisations of numerator and denominator.
    """
    def ln_rational(num: int, den: int, weight: Fraction) -> LogCombo:
        out: LogCombo = {}
        for value, sign in ((num, 1), (den, -1)):
            m = value
            f = 2
            while f * f <= m:
                while m % f == 0:
                    out[f] = out.get(f, Fraction(0)) + sign * weight
                    m //= f
                f += 1
            if m > 1:
                out[m] = out.get(m, Fraction(0)) + sign * weight
        return out

    plus_num, plus_den = n + 2, n            # 1 + 2/n
    minus_num, minus_den = n - 2, n          # 1 - 2/n
    combo = combo_sub(
        ln_rational(plus_num, plus_den, Fraction(n + 2, n)),
        {b: -c for b, c in ln_rational(minus_num, minus_den,
                                       Fraction(n - 2, n)).items()},
    )
    return combo, Fraction(2)


def ambiguity_combo(n: int) -> Tuple[LogCombo, Fraction]:
    """Return (C, s) such that A(n) = (sum over C) / (s * ln 2), i.e. ln n / (n^2 ln 2)."""
    combo: LogCombo = {}
    m, f = n, 2
    while f * f <= m:
        while m % f == 0:
            combo[f] = combo.get(f, Fraction(0)) + 1
            m //= f
        f += 1
    if m > 1:
        combo[m] = combo.get(m, Fraction(0)) + 1
    return combo, Fraction(n * n)

    a_combo, a_scale = ambiguity_combo(n)

    lhs = {b: c / a_scale for b, c in a_combo.items()}
    rhs = {b: c / x_scale for b, c in x_combo.items()}
    L, R, verdict, D = integer_certificate(lhs, rhs)
    label = f"A({n}) < X({n})"
    return label, L, R, verdict, D

<script>
const LN2 = Math.log(2), LOG2E = 1/LN2;
const CAP = 2*LOG2E, GAP = LOG2E - 1, RATIO = 2/(1-LN2);
const log2 = x => Math.log(x)/LN2;

function X(n){ const p = 0.5 + 1/n, q = 1-p;
  const H = -(p>0? p*log2(p):0) - (q>0? q*log2(q):0); return 1 - H; }
function A(n){ return log2(n)/(n*n); }
function g(n){ const u = 1/(n*n); return -(1-u)*log2(1-u) - u; }
function R(n){ const v = 4/(n*n); return v>=1 ? Infinity : -0.5*log2(1-v); }

const fmt = (x,d=9) => (x===Infinity? "∞" : x.toExponential? (Math.abs(x)<1e-4 && x!==0 ? x.toExponential(4) : x.toFixed(d)) : x);
const sci = x => (x===Infinity? "∞" : x.toExponential(3));

const slider = document.getElementById('slider');

function nFromSlider(v){
  const t = v/1000;                       // 0..1
  return Math.max(2, Math.round(2*Math.pow(500000, t)));
}

function draw(n){
  const c = document.getElementById('plot'), ctx = c.getContext('2d');
  const W = c.width, Hh = c.height, L = 60, Rr = 20, T = 18, B = 38;
  ctx.clearRect(0,0,W,Hh);
  const nmin = 4, nmax = 20;
  const xs = v => L + (v-nmin)/(nmax-nmin)*(W-L-Rr);
  const ymax = 0.20;
  const ys = v => T + (1 - v/ymax)*(Hh-T-B);

  // shaded certified window
  ctx.fillStyle = "rgba(199,146,234,.13)";
  ctx.fillRect(xs(7), T, xs(8)-xs(7), Hh-T-B);

  // axes + grid
  ctx.strokeStyle = "#232b47"; ctx.lineWidth = 1; ctx.fillStyle = "#98a3c4";
  ctx.font = "12px ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace";
  for(let k=nmin;k<=nmax;k+=2){
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(xs(k),T); ctx.lineTo(xs(k),Hh-B); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillText(String(k), xs(k)-6, Hh-B+18);
  }
  for(let y=0;y<=ymax+1e-9;y+=0.05){
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(L,ys(y)); ctx.lineTo(W-Rr,ys(y)); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillText(y.toFixed(2), 14, ys(y)+4);
  }
  ctx.fillText("resolution n", W/2-40, Hh-6);

  // curves
  const curve = (f,color) => {
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.strokeStyle = color; ctx.lineWidth = 2.4;
    for(let i=0;i<=600;i++){
      const v = nmin + (nmax-nmin)*i/600, y = f(v);
      const px = xs(v), py = ys(y);
      i? ctx.lineTo(px,py) : ctx.moveTo(px,py);
    }
    ctx.stroke();
  };
  curve(A, "#ffd166");
  curve(X, "#5ad1ff");

  // integer markers
  for(let k=nmin;k<=nmax;k++){
    ctx.fillStyle="#ffd166"; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(xs(k),ys(A(k)),3,0,7); ctx.fill();
    ctx.fillStyle="#5ad1ff"; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(xs(k),ys(X(k)),3,0,7); ctx.fill();
  }

  // crossing point
  let lo=7, hi=8;
  for(let i=0;i<80;i++){ const m=(lo+hi)/2; if((A(lo)-X(lo))*(A(m)-X(m))<=0) hi=m; else lo=m; }
  const nstar=(lo+hi)/2;
  ctx.strokeStyle="#e8ecf8"; ctx.setLineDash([4,4]); ctx.lineWidth=1;
  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(xs(nstar),T); ctx.lineTo(xs(nstar),Hh-B); ctx.stroke();
  ctx.setLineDash([]);
  ctx.fillStyle="#e8ecf8"; ctx.fillText("n* = "+nstar.toFixed(6), xs(nstar)+8, T+16);

  // current n marker (if inside the window)
  if(n>=nmin && n<=nmax){
    ctx.strokeStyle="#c792ea"; ctx.lineWidth=2;
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(xs(n),T); ctx.lineTo(xs(n),Hh-B); ctx.stroke();
  }
  return nstar;
}

# The Four Fork Channels — a guided tour

> **What you will learn.** How four apparently interchangeable ways of measuring a vanishing
> bias turn out to have four *different* exact constants; why a perfectly reasonable guess
> about their ratio was wrong by a factor of $3.2589$; and how a question about transcendental
> entropies can be settled by comparing two $85$-digit integers.

---

## 1. The situation: a coin that is almost fair

Fix an integer **resolution** $n \ge 2$ and consider a coin that lands heads with probability
$$p_n = \frac12 + \frac1n .$$
At $n = 2$ the coin always lands heads. At $n = 655360$ it is fair for all practical purposes.
Alongside the coin, think of a rare **fork event** of probability $1/n^2$ — the branch point
that gives the family its name.

The engine of everything below is the **binary entropy function**
$$H(p) = -p\log_2 p - (1-p)\log_2(1-p),$$
the average surprise, in bits, of one flip of a $p$-coin. It peaks at $H(\tfrac12) = 1$ and
falls to $0$ at the two certainties.

<details>
<summary><b>Refresher: why entropy is measured in bits</b></summary>

An event of probability $q$ carries surprisal $\log_2(1/q)$ bits: an event with $q = 1/8$
"costs" $3$ bits to describe, because there are $8$ equally likely alternatives and $3$ binary
questions separate them. Entropy is the average surprisal over the outcomes. A fair coin
averages one bit; any bias makes the outcome more predictable and lowers the average. Good
background reading: [entropy in information theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entropy_(information_theory))
and [Kullback–Leibler divergence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kullback%E2%80%93Leibler_divergence).
</details>

Four channels measure the fork's asymmetry:

| channel | definition | what it measures |
|---|---|---|
| capacity $X(n)$ | $1 - H\!\left(\tfrac12 + \tfrac1n\right)$ | bits lost relative to a fair coin |
| ambiguity $A(n)$ | $\log_2 n / n^2$ | weighted surprisal of the fork event |
| gap $g(n)$ | $-(1-\tfrac1{n^2})\log_2(1-\tfrac1{n^2}) - \tfrac1{n^2}$ | entropy of the survival branch, minus the fork probability |
| reverse $R(n)$ | $-\tfrac12\log_2\!\left(1-\tfrac4{n^2}\right)$ | the same distance, measured the other way round |

and the **isolation channel** is $\mathrm{Is}(n) = A(n) + R(n)$.

All four vanish. The question is: multiplied by $n^2$, what do they converge to?

---

## 2. Play with it first

Drag the resolution slider. Watch the middle column ($\times\,n^2$) settle onto four constants,
watch the ratio $X/g$ walk past $2$ and stop at $6.5178$, and watch the ambiguity curve
overtake the capacity curve somewhere between $7$ and $8$.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

Three things are worth noticing before we prove anything.

1. **Three of the four rescaled channels converge to a bare constant** — no $\log n$ anywhere.
2. **The ambiguity channel is different**: $A(n)\,n^2 = \log_2 n$ exactly, so it escapes upwards.
3. **The gap channel is much smaller than the others**, and its constant $0.442695$ looks like
   nothing in particular — until you notice that $\log_2 e = 1.442695$.

---

## 3. The four exact laws

Writing $\log_2 e = 1/\ln 2 = 1.4426950\ldots$:

$$g(n)\,n^2 \longrightarrow \log_2 e - 1 = 0.442695\ldots$$
$$X(n)\,n^2 \longrightarrow 2\log_2 e = 2.885390\ldots$$
$$\frac{A(n)\,n^2}{\log_2 n} = 1 \quad\text{exactly, for every } n\ge2$$
$$\bigl(\mathrm{Is}(n)-A(n)\bigr)n^2 \longrightarrow 2\log_2 e = 2.885390\ldots$$

That third one is not a limit statement at all — it is an identity, since
$A(n)n^2 = \log_2 n$ by definition. The fourth says the *reverse* distance from fair to biased
has the *same* leading constant as the *forward* distance, even though the two differ at every
finite $n$.

<details>
<summary><b>Click to reveal the proofs (they are shorter than you expect)</b></summary>

Everything rests on two elementary windows.

**Window 1.** For $u<1$, $\;u \le -\ln(1-u)$, and for $u \le \tfrac12$, $\;-\ln(1-u) \le u+2u^2$.
*Proof:* the first is $\ln t \le t-1$ at $t = 1-u$; the second is the same inequality at
$t = (1-u)^{-1}$, together with $\tfrac{1}{1-u} \le 1 + u + 2u^2$, which after clearing the
denominator reads $1 \le 1 + u^2(1-2u)$.

**Gap law.** With $u = n^{-2}$ and $L = -\ln(1-u)$ one has $g(n)n^2 = \frac{(1-u)L}{u\ln2} - 1$,
so Window 1 traps the bracket within $u$ of $1$ and gives
$$\bigl|g(n)n^2 - (\log_2 e - 1)\bigr| \le \frac{1}{n\ln2}.$$
Note where the constant comes from: $L \approx u$, so the entropy term contributes
$u\log_2 e$ and the definition then subtracts a whole $u$ — leaving $u(\log_2 e - 1)$.

**Reverse law.** Identical, with $v = 4/n^2$: $\;|R(n)n^2 - 2\log_2 e| \le 16/(n\ln 2)$.

**Capacity law.** Here the leading term is quadratic, so one order more is needed. The key
identity is
$$X(n) = \frac{F(2/n)}{2\ln 2}, \qquad F(x) = (1+x)\ln(1+x) + (1-x)\ln(1-x),$$
obtained by writing $\tfrac12+\tfrac1n = \tfrac{1+2/n}{2}$ and letting the two $\ln 2$ terms
cancel the leading $1$. Since $|\ln(1+x) - (x - x^2/2)| \le 2|x|^3$ for $|x|\le\tfrac12$, adding
the two halves of $F$ (the linear terms cancel, the quadratic ones combine) gives
$|F(x) - x^2| \le 6|x|^3$, hence
$$\bigl|X(n)n^2 - 2\log_2 e\bigr| \le \frac{24}{n\ln2}.$$
</details>

---

## 4. The ratio that refuted a guess

Divide the capacity law by the gap law:

$$\frac{X(n)}{g(n)} \longrightarrow \frac{2\log_2 e}{\log_2 e - 1} = \frac{2}{1-\ln 2} = 6.5177827\ldots$$

The pre-data prediction was $X/g \to 2$. It failed for one reason, and it is a reason worth
internalising: **the gap channel's definition subtracts a full unit from its own leading
coefficient.** The entropy piece contributes $\log_2 e = 1.442695$; the definition removes $1$;
what survives is $0.442695$, less than a third of what went in. Ratios against a channel that
has suffered such a near-cancellation are inflated by exactly $1/(1-\ln 2) = 3.258891$.

$$\underbrace{\frac{2\log_2 e}{\log_2 e}}_{=\,2\ \text{(the guess)}} \qquad\text{versus}\qquad \underbrace{\frac{2\log_2 e}{\log_2 e - 1}}_{=\,6.5178\ \text{(the truth)}}$$

Let us watch it happen numerically, together with all four laws and the *proved* error bounds
(the demo checks each observed error against its guaranteed bound at every resolution):

The picture below puts the whole story on one page: the rescaled channels flattening onto their

---

## 6. Computing the channels without losing digits

The gap channel is a difference of two quantities that agree to relative order $1/n^2$, so
ordinary double precision loses roughly $2\log_{10} n$ digits: by $n = 10^8$ there is nothing
left. The routine below evaluates all four channels in arbitrary precision and, at every
resolution, checks the answers against the proved rate bounds — so its output validates itself.

{{algorithm:0}}

<details>
<summary><b>Why catastrophic cancellation bites here</b></summary>

If $a$ and $b$ agree to $k$ significant digits, then $a - b$ computed in floating point retains
only $p - k$ of the $p$ digits you started with. In $g(n)$ the two terms
$-(1-u)\log_2(1-u)$ and $u$ agree to about $2\log_{10} n$ digits, and that is exactly the
accuracy you lose. See [loss of significance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catastrophic_cancellation).
The fix used here is simply to carry $50$ digits, but a numerically nicer route is to evaluate
$g$ through its series $g(n) = u(\log_2 e - 1) - \tfrac{u^2}{2}\log_2 e + \cdots$, in which no
cancellation occurs at all.
</details>

---

## 7. Where ambiguity overtakes capacity — an exact answer

Since $A(n)n^2 = \log_2 n \to \infty$ while $X(n)n^2 \to 2.885390$, the ratio $A/X$ tends to
infinity; and since $A(2)/X(2) = 1/4$, the two curves must cross. They cross exactly once, and
the crossing is pinned by two integer inequalities:

$$A(7) < X(7) \iff 7^{100} < 3^{126}\cdot 5^{35}, \qquad X(8) < A(8) \iff 5^{40}\cdot 3^{24} < 2^{131}.$$

The real crossing point is $n^\ast = 7.5681918\ldots$

Why bother with integers when a calculator says $A(7)/X(7) = 0.9595$? Because the margins are
a few percent, and because an inequality between logarithms of integers can be turned into an
inequality between integers *exactly* — clearing the common denominator of the rational
coefficients and exponentiating. No rounding, no error analysis, no doubt. The algorithm below
performs that reduction automatically for any resolution, and reproduces the two certificates
above verbatim.

{{algorithm:1}}

<details>
<summary><b>The reduction, step by step, at $n = 8$</b></summary>

At $n = 8$ we have $A(8) = \log_2 8/64 = 3/64$, and
$$X(8) = \frac{F(1/4)}{2\ln 2}, \qquad F(1/4) = \tfrac54\bigl(\ln 5 - 2\ln 2\bigr) + \tfrac34\bigl(\ln 3 - 2\ln 2\bigr).$$
The inequality $X(8) < A(8)$ becomes, after multiplying by $2\ln2 \cdot 64 > 0$ and collecting,
$$80\ln 5 + 48 \ln 3 < 262 \ln 2 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 40\ln5 + 24\ln 3 < 131\ln 2,$$
and exponentiating gives $5^{40}\cdot3^{24} < 2^{131}$ — the comparison of a $40$-digit integer
with another $40$-digit integer, which a computer settles in microseconds and a determined
human could settle by hand.
</details>

---

## 8. The other end of the scale: collapse at $n = 2$

At $n = 2$ the coin becomes a certainty and the family fractures:

$$X(2) = 1, \qquad A(2) = \tfrac14, \qquad g(2) = \tfrac54 - \tfrac34\log_2 3 = 0.0612781\ldots,$$

while $R(2)$ and $\mathrm{Is}(2)$ are **infinite** — the argument $1 - 4/n^2$ vanishes there.
This is not a technical blemish but the content of the asymmetry: the forward distance from a
certainty to a fair coin is one bit, but the reverse distance is infinite, because the fair
coin insists on an outcome the certainty has ruled out.

---

## 9. What to take away

* Four channels, four constants: $\log_2 e - 1$, $2\log_2 e$, the identity $A n^2 = \log_2 n$,
  and $2\log_2 e$ again for the reverse direction.
* One ratio, $2/(1-\ln 2) = 6.5178$, and one refuted guess, $2$.
* One mechanism behind the refutation: a definition that subtracts a leading term leaves a
  *difference* of constants, and differences remember nothing about the tidy factors that
  produced them.
* Two techniques worth stealing: squeezing a limit between two crude log windows to get the
  constant *and* an explicit rate, and converting a delicate inequality between logarithms
  into an exact comparison of integers.

This file formalises, from scratch and with complete proofs, the "exact constant laws"
of a four–channel *fork* model built out of the binary entropy function.

For a resolution parameter `n ≥ 2` we consider four scalar channels:

* the **capacity channel** `X n = 1 - H(1/2 + 1/n)`
  (equivalently the forward divergence `D(Bern(1/2+1/n) ‖ Bern(1/2))`),
* the **ambiguity channel** `A n = log₂ n / n²`
  (half the surprisal of a fork event of probability `1/n²`),
* the **gap channel** `g n = -(1 - 1/n²)·log₂(1 - 1/n²) - 1/n²`
  (the excess of the survival entropy term over the fork probability),
* the **reverse channel** `R n = -(1/2)·log₂(1 - 4/n²)`
  (the reverse divergence `D(Bern(1/2) ‖ Bern(1/2+1/n))`), and the
  **isolation channel** `Is n = A n + R n`.

The four exact constant laws proved below are

* `gch_mul_sq_tendsto`      : `g·n² → log₂ e - 1 = 0.442695…`  (no logarithmic factor),
* `Xch_mul_sq_tendsto`      : `X·n² → 2 log₂ e = 2.885390…`,
* `Ach_scaled_eq_one`       : `A·n²/log₂ n = 1` exactly, hence `→ 1`,
* `Isch_sub_Ach_mul_sq_tendsto` : `(Is - A)·n² → 2 log₂ e`,

and consequently

* `Xch_div_gch_tendsto`     : `X/g → 2 log₂ e/(log₂ e - 1) = 2/(1 - log 2) = 6.51778…`,

* `Xch_two`, `Ach_two`, `gch_two` : the values at the collapse point `n = 2`,
* `Ach_seven_lt_Xch_seven` and `Xch_eight_lt_Ach_eight` : the `A/X` sign flip happens

import Mathlib

namespace Catalog.Combinatorics.ForkChannel

open Real Filter Topology

noncomputable section

/-- Binary logarithm. -/
def lb (x : ℝ) : ℝ := Real.logb 2 x

/-- Binary entropy (in bits). -/
def binEnt (p : ℝ) : ℝ := -p * lb p - (1 - p) * lb (1 - p)

/-- The capacity channel `X n = 1 - H(1/2 + 1/n)`. -/
def Xch (n : ℝ) : ℝ := 1 - binEnt (1 / 2 + 1 / n)

/-- The ambiguity channel `A n = log₂ n / n²`. -/
def Ach (n : ℝ) : ℝ := lb n / n ^ 2

/-- The gap channel `g n = -(1 - 1/n²) log₂(1 - 1/n²) - 1/n²`. -/
def gch (n : ℝ) : ℝ := -(1 - 1 / n ^ 2) * lb (1 - 1 / n ^ 2) - 1 / n ^ 2

/-- The reverse-divergence channel `R n = -(1/2) log₂(1 - 4/n²)`. -/
def Rch (n : ℝ) : ℝ := -(1 / 2) * lb (1 - 4 / n ^ 2)

/-- The isolation channel `Is n = A n + R n`. -/
def Isch (n : ℝ) : ℝ := Ach n + Rch n

/-! ### Elementary logarithm windows -/

lemma log_two_pos : 0 < Real.log 2 := Real.log_pos (by norm_num)

lemma log_two_lt_one : Real.log 2 < 1 := by
  have h := Real.log_lt_sub_one_of_pos (x := 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
  linarith

/-- Lower window: `u ≤ -log (1-u)` for `u < 1`. -/
lemma neg_log_one_sub_ge {u : ℝ} (hu : u < 1) : u ≤ -Real.log (1 - u) := by

  linarith

  rw [Real.log_inv] at h
  have hle : (1:ℝ) / (1 - u) ≤ 1 + u + 2 * u ^ 2 := by
    rw [div_le_iff₀ hpos]; nlinarith
  rw [inv_eq_one_div] at h
  linarith

  have hsum : (∑ i ∈ Finset.range 2, (-x) ^ (i + 1) / ((i : ℝ) + 1)) = -x + x ^ 2 / 2 := by
    simp [Finset.sum_range_succ]; ring
  rw [hsum, show (1 : ℝ) - -x = 1 + x from by ring, abs_neg] at h
  have hx0 : (0:ℝ) ≤ |x| := abs_nonneg x
  have hden : (1 : ℝ) / 2 ≤ 1 - |x| := by linarith

    exact h

  linarith

/-- The symmetrised fork function. -/

about at large n).

The four channels, for a resolution parameter n >= 2 (all logs base 2):

    H(p)   = -p log2 p - (1-p) log2 (1-p)          binary entropy
    X(n)   = 1 - H(1/2 + 1/n)                      capacity channel
    A(n)   = log2 n / n^2                          ambiguity channel
    g(n)   = -(1 - 1/n^2) log2(1 - 1/n^2) - 1/n^2  gap channel
    R(n)   = -(1/2) log2(1 - 4/n^2)                reverse channel  (n > 2)
    Is(n)  = A(n) + R(n)                           isolation channel

The exact constant laws demonstrated here:

    g(n)  * n^2               -> log2 e - 1 = 0.442695...
    X(n)  * n^2               -> 2 log2 e   = 2.885390...
    A(n)  * n^2 / log2 n      == 1          (identically, for every n >= 2)
    (Is(n) - A(n)) * n^2      -> 2 log2 e   = 2.885390...
    X(n)  / g(n)              -> 2/(1 - ln 2) = 6.517782...   (NOT 2)
    A(n)  / X(n)              -> infinity

with proved finite-n rates

    |g(n) n^2 - (log2 e - 1)| <= 1/(n ln 2)          (n >= 2)
    |X(n) n^2 - 2 log2 e|     <= 24/(n ln 2)         (n >= 4)
    |R(n) n^2 - 2 log2 e|     <= 16/(n ln 2)         (n >= 4)

and the exact small-n structure

    X(2) = 1,  A(2) = 1/4,  g(2) = 5/4 - (3/4) log2 3 = 0.0612781...
    R, Is diverge at n = 2
    A(7) < X(7) and X(8) < A(8), certified by  7^100 < 3^126 * 5^35
                                          and  5^40 * 3^24 < 2^131.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from decimal import Decimal, getcontext
from typing import Callable, List, Optional, Tuple

getcontext().prec = 60  # working precision in decimal digits

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Constants
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

LN2: Decimal = Decimal(2).ln()
LOG2E: Decimal = Decimal(1) / LN2          # 1.4426950408889634...
GAP_CONST: Decimal = LOG2E - 1             # 0.4426950408889634...
CAP_CONST: Decimal = 2 * LOG2E             # 2.8853900817779268...
RATIO_CONST: Decimal = Decimal(2) / (1 - LN2)  # 6.5177827065418...


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The four channels
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def log2(x: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    """Binary logarithm at working precision."""
    return x.ln() / LN2


def binary_entropy(p: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    """H(p) = -p log2 p - (1-p) log2 (1-p), with the convention 0 log2 0 = 0."""
    q = Decimal(1) - p
    term_p = Decimal(0) if p == 0 else -p * log2(p)
    term_q = Decimal(0) if q == 0 else -q * log2(q)
    return term_p + term_q


def capacity_channel(n: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    """X(n) = 1 - H(1/2 + 1/n): bits lost relative to a fair coin."""
    return Decimal(1) - binary_entropy(Decimal(1) / 2 + Decimal(1) / n)


def ambiguity_channel(n: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    """A(n) = log2 n / n^2."""
    return log2(n) / (n * n)


def gap_channel(n: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    """g(n) = -(1 - 1/n^2) log2(1 - 1/n^2) - 1/n^2."""
    u = Decimal(1) / (n * n)
    return -(Decimal(1) - u) * log2(Decimal(1) - u) - u


def reverse_channel(n: Decimal) -> Optional[Decimal]:
    """R(n) = -(1/2) log2(1 - 4/n^2); undefined (infinite) at n = 2."""
    v = Decimal(4) / (n * n)
    if v >= 1:
        return None
    return -(Decimal(1) / 2) * log2(Decimal(1) - v)


def isolation_channel(n: Decimal) -> Optional[Decimal]:
    """Is(n) = A(n) + R(n)."""
    r = reverse_channel(n)
    return None if r is None else ambiguity_channel(n) + r


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The fork function, and the closed form X(n) = F(2/n) / (2 ln 2)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def fork_function(x: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    """F(x) = (1+x) ln(1+x) + (1-x) ln(1-x); even, non-negative, F(x) = x^2 + O(x^4)."""
    return (1 + x) * (1 + x).ln() + (1 - x) * (1 - x).ln()


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reporting helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def fmt(x: Optional[Decimal], digits: int = 9) -> str:
    if x is None:
        return "        inf"
    return f"{float(x):>{digits + 4}.{digits}f}"


def rule(title: str) -> None:
    print()
    print("=" * 78)
    print(title)
    print("=" * 78)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 1 — the master table of the four channels
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_table(ns: List[int]) -> None:
    rule("1. The four channels, rescaled by n^2")
    print(f"{'n':>8}  {'X n^2':>13}  {'g n^2':>13}  {'A n^2/log2 n':>13}"
          f"  {'R n^2':>13}  {'X/g':>10}  {'A/X':>10}")
    for k in ns:
        n = Decimal(k)
        nsq = n * n
        X = capacity_channel(n)
        A = ambiguity_channel(n)
        g = gap_channel(n)
        R = reverse_channel(n)
        print(f"{k:>8}  {fmt(X * nsq)}  {fmt(g * nsq)}  "
              f"{fmt(A * nsq / log2(n))}  {fmt(R * nsq if R is not None else None)}  "
              f"{float(X / g):>10.5f}  {float(A / X):>10.5f}")
    print(f"{'limit':>8}  {fmt(CAP_CONST)}  {fmt(GAP_CONST)}  {fmt(Decimal(1))}  "
          f"{fmt(CAP_CONST)}  {float(RATIO_CONST):>10.5f}  {'inf':>10}")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 2 — the exact constants and the refuted guess
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_constants(n_big: int = 655360) -> None:
    rule("2. The exact constants (and the refutation of X/g -> 2)")
    n = Decimal(n_big)
    nsq = n * n
    X, A, g = capacity_channel(n), ambiguity_channel(n), gap_channel(n)
    R = reverse_channel(n)
    assert R is not None
    Is = A + R

    rows: List[Tuple[str, Decimal, Decimal]] = [
        ("g * n^2        -> log2 e - 1", g * nsq, GAP_CONST),
        ("X * n^2        -> 2 log2 e  ", X * nsq, CAP_CONST),
        ("A * n^2/log2 n == 1         ", A * nsq / log2(n), Decimal(1)),
        ("(Is - A) * n^2 -> 2 log2 e  ", (Is - A) * nsq, CAP_CONST),
        ("X / g          -> 2/(1-ln2) ", X / g, RATIO_CONST),
    ]
    print(f"evaluated at n = {n_big} with {getcontext().prec}-digit arithmetic\n")
    print(f"{'law':<30}  {'computed':>20}  {'constant':>20}  {'|deviation|':>12}")
    for name, computed, target in rows:
        dev = abs(computed - target)
        print(f"{name:<30}  {float(computed):>20.12f}  {float(target):>20.12f}"
              f"  {float(dev):>12.3e}")

    print()
    print(f"pre-data guess  X/g -> 2          : deviation "
          f"{float(abs(X / g - 2)):.6f}   REFUTED")
    print(f"corrected law   X/g -> 2/(1-ln 2) : deviation "
          f"{float(abs(X / g - RATIO_CONST)):.3e}   confirmed")
    print()
    print("Why 6.5178 and not 2 — the near-cancellation inside g:")
    print(f"  entropy term alone contributes  log2 e     = {float(LOG2E):.6f}")
    print(f"  the definition subtracts        1          = 1.000000")
    print(f"  leaving                         log2 e - 1 = {float(GAP_CONST):.6f}")
    print(f"  so the ratio is inflated by 1/(1-ln 2)     = "
          f"{float(1 / (1 - LN2)):.6f}  (2 x this = {float(RATIO_CONST):.6f})")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 3 — the proved finite-n rate bounds
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_rates(ns: List[int]) -> None:
    rule("3. Proved finite-n error bounds versus observed errors")
    print(f"{'n':>8}  {'|g n^2 - c_g|':>14} {'bound 1/(n ln2)':>16} "
          f"{'|X n^2 - c_X|':>14} {'bound 24/(n ln2)':>17} "
          f"{'|R n^2 - c_X|':>14} {'bound 16/(n ln2)':>17}")
    for k in ns:
        n = Decimal(k)
        nsq = n * n
        eg = abs(gap_channel(n) * nsq - GAP_CONST)
        eX = abs(capacity_channel(n) * nsq - CAP_CONST)
        R = reverse_channel(n)
        eR = abs(R * nsq - CAP_CONST) if R is not None else None
        bg, bX, bR = 1 / (n * LN2), 24 / (n * LN2), 16 / (n * LN2)
        ok = (eg <= bg) and (eX <= bX or k < 4) and (eR is None or eR <= bR or k < 4)
        print(f"{k:>8}  {float(eg):>14.3e} {float(bg):>16.3e} "
              f"{float(eX):>14.3e} {float(bX):>17.3e} "
              f"{(float(eR) if eR is not None else float('inf')):>14.3e} "
              f"{float(bR):>17.3e}   {'ok' if ok else '!!'}")
    print("\n(The bounds are deliberately crude: the true errors are O(1/n^2),")
    print(" because the underlying fork function F(x) = (1+x)ln(1+x)+(1-x)ln(1-x) is even.)")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 4 — collapse at n = 2
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_collapse() -> None:
    rule("4. The collapse point n = 2")
    two = Decimal(2)
    X2, A2, g2 = capacity_channel(two), ambiguity_channel(two), gap_channel(two)
    g2_exact = Decimal(5) / 4 - (Decimal(3) / 4) * log2(Decimal(3))
    print(f"  X(2) = {float(X2):.12f}   (exact value 1: the coin is a certainty, H(1) = 0)")
    print(f"  A(2) = {float(A2):.12f}   (exact value 1/4)")
    print(f"  g(2) = {float(g2):.12f}   (exact value 5/4 - (3/4) log2 3 = "
          f"{float(g2_exact):.12f})")
    print(f"  g(2) * 4 = {float(g2 * 4):.12f}   (matches the tabulated g*n^2 at n = 2)")
    print(f"  R(2) : {reverse_channel(two)}   -- diverges: 1 - 4/n^2 = 0 at n = 2")
    print(f"  Is(2): {isolation_channel(two)}   -- diverges for the same reason")
    print()
    print("  Note: the forward divergence from a certainty to a fair coin is one bit,")
    print("  but the reverse divergence is infinite, since the fair coin gives positive")
    print("  probability to an event the certainty declares impossible.")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 5 — the A/X crossing in (7,8) with integer certificates
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_crossing() -> None:
    rule("5. The A/X sign flip lies exactly in the window (7, 8)")
    for k in range(2, 13):
        n = Decimal(k)
        A, X = ambiguity_channel(n), capacity_channel(n)
        mark = "A < X" if A < X else "A > X"
        print(f"  n = {k:>2}:  A = {float(A):.9f}   X = {float(X):.9f}   "
              f"A/X = {float(A / X):.6f}   {mark}")

    print("\n  Integer certificates (exact arithmetic, no floating point):")
    lhs7, rhs7 = 7 ** 100, 3 ** 126 * 5 ** 35
    lhs8, rhs8 = 5 ** 40 * 3 ** 24, 2 ** 131
    print(f"    A(7) < X(7)  <=>  7^100 < 3^126 * 5^35")
    print(f"        7^100        = {lhs7}")
    print(f"        3^126 * 5^35 = {rhs7}")
    print(f"        holds: {lhs7 < rhs7}")
    print(f"    X(8) < A(8)  <=>  5^40 * 3^24 < 2^131")
    print(f"        5^40 * 3^24  = {lhs8}")
    print(f"        2^131        = {rhs8}")
    print(f"        holds: {lhs8 < rhs8}")

    # Locate the real crossing point by bisection on A - X.
    lo, hi = Decimal(7), Decimal(8)
    f: Callable[[Decimal], Decimal] = lambda t: ambiguity_channel(t) - capacity_channel(t)
    for _ in range(80):
        mid = (lo + hi) / 2
        if f(lo) * f(mid) <= 0:
            hi = mid
        else:
            lo = mid
    print(f"\n  Real crossing point n* = {float((lo + hi) / 2):.12f}  (bisection in (7,8))")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstration 6 — the closed form X(n) = F(2/n)/(2 ln 2) and its cubic window
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_fork_identity(ns: List[int]) -> None:
    rule("6. The closed form X(n) = F(2/n)/(2 ln 2) and the cubic window |F(x)-x^2| <= 6|x|^3")
    print(f"{'n':>8}  {'X(n)':>18}  {'F(2/n)/(2 ln2)':>18}  {'|difference|':>13}"
          f"  {'|F(x)-x^2|':>12}  {'6|x|^3':>12}")
    for k in ns:
        n = Decimal(k)
        x = Decimal(2) / n
        lhs = capacity_channel(n)
        rhs = fork_function(x) / (2 * LN2)
        err = abs(fork_function(x) - x * x)
        bnd = 6 * abs(x) ** 3
        print(f"{k:>8}  {float(lhs):>18.14f}  {float(rhs):>18.14f}  "
              f"{float(abs(lhs - rhs)):>13.3e}  {float(err):>12.3e}  {float(bnd):>12.3e}")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main() -> None:
    print(__doc__)
    demo_table([2, 3, 4, 7, 8, 16, 17, 100, 1000, 100000, 655360])
    demo_constants(655360)
    demo_rates([2, 4, 8, 16, 100, 1000, 100000, 655360])
    demo_collapse()
    demo_crossing()
    demo_fork_identity([4, 8, 16, 100, 1000, 100000])
    rule("All demonstrated laws agree with the proved statements.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

concept.title: Riemann Convergence of Bhattacharyya Angle Sums
concept.concept_description:
The discrete bound by sums of Bhattacharyya angles is now proved. The remaining question is calibration: do those sums converge to the Fisher-Rao length as the partition mesh tends to zero? A positive answer identifies the Fisher-Rao length functional with the length structure of the spherical metric of the square-root embedding, and implies the geodesic lower bound.

For a C¹ curve of strictly positive probability vectors on [a,b], the sums ∑ₖ 2·arccos BC(p_{t_k}, p_{t_{k+1}}) over partitions converge to fisherRaoLength p v a b as the mesh tends to 0.

Establish the local expansion 2 arccos BC(p_s, p_t) = ∫_s^t speed + O((t−s)³) using the chord bound and the exact two-point evaluation, then sum over a partition and pass to the limit.

The Fisher-Rao length becomes the intrinsic length of the spherical metric, and the geodesic lower bound 2 arccos BC ≤ length follows immediately.

The integral functional would not be the induced length of the Bhattacharyya angle metric, indicating that the definition of fisherRaoLength needs a different normalisation.

  exact congrArg Real.sqrt (Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by
    simp [Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs])

omit [Fintype ι] in
theorem continuous_sqrtVelVec {p v : ℝ → ι → ℝ}
    (hderiv : ∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun s => p s i) (v t i) t)
    (hv : ∀ i, Continuous fun t => v t i) (hpos : ∀ t i, 0 < p t i) :
    Continuous (sqrtVelVec p v) := by
  have h : Continuous fun t => (sqrtVel p v t : ι → ℝ) :=
    continuous_pi fun i => continuous_sqrtVel hderiv hv hpos i
  exact (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℝ).symm.continuous.comp h

/-! ## Elementary facts about the length functional -/

/-- Additivity of the Fisher–Rao length along a finite chain of parameters. -/
theorem fisherRaoLength_sum_partition {p v : ℝ → ι → ℝ}
    (hderiv : ∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun s => p s i) (v t i) t)
    (hv : ∀ i, Continuous fun t => v t i) (hpos : ∀ t i, 0 < p t i)
    (T : ℕ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) :
    ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, fisherRaoLength p v (T k) (T (k + 1))
      = fisherRaoLength p v (T 0) (T N) := by
  induction N with
  | zero => simp [fisherRaoLength]
  | succ n ih =>
      rw [Finset.sum_range_succ, ih]
      exact fisherRaoLength_add hderiv hv hpos

/-- A speed bound integrates to a length bound. -/
theorem fisherRaoLength_le_of_speed_le {p v : ℝ → ι → ℝ}
    (hderiv : ∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun s => p s i) (v t i) t)
    (hv : ∀ i, Continuous fun t => v t i) (hpos : ∀ t i, 0 < p t i)
    {s t M : ℝ} (hst : s ≤ t) (hM : ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc s t, fisherRaoSpeed (p r) (v r) ≤ M) :
    fisherRaoLength p v s t ≤ M * (t - s) := by
  have hcont := continuous_fisherRaoSpeed hderiv hv hpos
  have hconst : IntervalIntegrable (fun _ : ℝ => M) volume s t := _root_.intervalIntegrable_const
  have := intervalIntegral.integral_mono_on hst (hcont.intervalIntegrable s t) hconst hM
  simpa [fisherRaoLength, mul_comm] using this

/-! ## The geodesic bound -/

/-- **Geodesic bound.**  Twice the Bhattacharyya angle between the endpoints of
a `C¹` curve of positive probability vectors is at most its Fisher–Rao length:
the Fisher–Rao length dominates the spherical distance of the square-root
embeddings. -/
theorem two_arccos_bhattacharyya_le_fisherRaoLength {p v : ℝ → ι → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b)
    (hderiv : ∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun s => p s i) (v t i) t)
    (hv : ∀ i, Continuous fun t => v t i) (hpos : ∀ t i, 0 < p t i)
    (hp1 : ∀ t, ∑ i, p t i = 1) :
    2 * arccos (bhattacharyya (p a) (p b)) ≤ fisherRaoLength p v a b := by
  set θ : ℝ := arccos (bhattacharyya (p a) (p b)) with hθdef
  have hθ0 : 0 ≤ θ := Real.arccos_nonneg _
  have hL0 : 0 ≤ fisherRaoLength p v a b := fisherRaoLength_nonneg p v hab
  -- a uniform speed bound on `[a,b]`
  obtain ⟨M, hM0, hM⟩ : ∃ M : ℝ, 0 ≤ M ∧ ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc a b, fisherRaoSpeed (p r) (v r) ≤ M := by
    obtain ⟨x, _, hmax⟩ := (isCompact_Icc (a := a) (b := b)).exists_isMaxOn
      ⟨a, Set.left_mem_Icc.mpr hab⟩
      (continuous_fisherRaoSpeed hderiv hv hpos).continuousOn
    exact ⟨fisherRaoSpeed (p x) (v x), fisherRaoSpeed_nonneg _ _, fun r hr => hmax hr⟩
  -- the key estimate for the uniform partition of `[a,b]` into `N` pieces
  have key : ∀ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N → θ * √(1 - (M * ((b - a) / N) / 4) ^ 2)
      ≤ fisherRaoLength p v a b / 2 := by
    intro N hN
    have hNpos : (0:ℝ) < N := by exact_mod_cast Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one hN
    set h : ℝ := (b - a) / N with hhdef
    have hh0 : 0 ≤ h := div_nonneg (by linarith) hNpos.le
    have hNh : (N : ℝ) * h = b - a := by rw [hhdef]; field_simp
    set T : ℕ → ℝ := fun k => a + k * h with hTdef
    have hT0 : T 0 = a := by simp [hTdef]
    have hTN : T N = b := by simp only [hTdef]; linarith
    have hstep : ∀ k : ℕ, T (k + 1) - T k = h := by
      intro k
      simp only [hTdef]
      push_cast
      ring
    have hmono : ∀ k : ℕ, T k ≤ T (k + 1) := fun k => by linarith [hstep k]
    have hmem : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ N → T k ∈ Set.Icc a b := by
      intro k hk
      have hkN : (k : ℝ) ≤ N := by exact_mod_cast hk
      have h1 : 0 ≤ (k : ℝ) * h := by positivity
      have h2 : (k : ℝ) * h ≤ (N : ℝ) * h := by nlinarith
      exact ⟨by simp only [hTdef]; linarith, by simp only [hTdef]; linarith⟩
    -- each piece of the subdivision is short
    have hLk : ∀ k : ℕ, k < N → fisherRaoLength p v (T k) (T (k + 1)) ≤ M * h := by
      intro k hk
      have hsub : ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc (T k) (T (k + 1)), fisherRaoSpeed (p r) (v r) ≤ M := fun r hr =>
        hM r ⟨le_trans (hmem k hk.le).1 hr.1, le_trans hr.2 (hmem (k + 1) hk).2⟩
      have hlen := fisherRaoLength_le_of_speed_le hderiv hv hpos (hmono k) hsub
      rwa [hstep k] at hlen
    have hLk0 : ∀ k : ℕ, 0 ≤ fisherRaoLength p v (T k) (T (k + 1)) := fun k =>
      fisherRaoLength_nonneg p v (hmono k)
    -- convert the chord bound on each piece into an angle bound, with a uniform factor
    set c : ℝ := √(1 - (M * h / 4) ^ 2) with hcdef
    have hc0 : 0 ≤ c := Real.sqrt_nonneg _
    have hpiece : ∀ k : ℕ, k < N →
        arccos (bhattacharyya (p (T k)) (p (T (k + 1)))) * c
          ≤ fisherRaoLength p v (T k) (T (k + 1)) / 2 := by
      intro k hk
      set Lk : ℝ := fisherRaoLength p v (T k) (T (k + 1)) with hLkdef
      have hchord := sqrt_chord_le_half_fisherRao_length (hmono k) hderiv hv hpos
      have hangle := arccos_bhattacharyya_mul_sqrt_le (p (T (k + 1))) (p (T k))
        (fun i => (hpos _ i).le) (fun i => (hpos _ i).le) (hp1 _) (hp1 _)
        (m := Lk / 2) (by linarith [hLk0 k]) (by linarith [hchord])
      rw [bhattacharyya_comm] at hangle
      have hle : c ≤ √(1 - (Lk / 2 / 2) ^ 2) := by
        refine Real.sqrt_le_sqrt ?_
        have h1 : Lk ≤ M * h := hLk k hk
        have h2 : 0 ≤ Lk := hLk0 k
        nlinarith
      have hθk : 0 ≤ arccos (bhattacharyya (p (T k)) (p (T (k + 1)))) := Real.arccos_nonneg _
      calc arccos (bhattacharyya (p (T k)) (p (T (k + 1)))) * c
          ≤ arccos (bhattacharyya (p (T k)) (p (T (k + 1)))) * √(1 - (Lk / 2 / 2) ^ 2) :=
            mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hle hθk
        _ ≤ Lk / 2 := hangle
    -- the spherical triangle inequality along the subdivision
    have htri : θ ≤ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, arccos (bhattacharyya (p (T k)) (p (T (k + 1)))) := by
      have hsum := arccos_bhattacharyya_le_sum (fun k => p (T k))
        (fun k i => (hpos _ i).le) (fun k => hp1 _) N
      rwa [hT0, hTN] at hsum
    have hsum : (∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, arccos (bhattacharyya (p (T k)) (p (T (k + 1))))) * c
        ≤ fisherRaoLength p v a b / 2 := by
      rw [Finset.sum_mul]
      have h1 : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, arccos (bhattacharyya (p (T k)) (p (T (k + 1)))) * c
          ≤ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, fisherRaoLength p v (T k) (T (k + 1)) / 2 :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum fun k hk => hpiece k (Finset.mem_range.mp hk)
      have h2 : ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, fisherRaoLength p v (T k) (T (k + 1)) / 2
          = fisherRaoLength p v a b / 2 := by
        rw [← Finset.sum_div, fisherRaoLength_sum_partition hderiv hv hpos T N, hT0, hTN]
      linarith
    have hmul := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right htri hc0
    linarith
  -- let the mesh tend to zero
  have hlim : Filter.Tendsto
      (fun N : ℕ => θ * √(1 - (M * ((b - a) / N) / 4) ^ 2)) Filter.atTop (nhds (θ * 1)) := by
    have h0 : Filter.Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (b - a) / N) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) :=
      tendsto_const_div_atTop_nhds_zero_nat (b - a)
    have hg : Filter.Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (M * ((b - a) / N) / 4) ^ 2) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) := by
      have h3 : Filter.Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => M * ((b - a) / N) / 4) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) := by
        simpa using (h0.const_mul M).div_const 4
      simpa using h3.pow 2
    have h1 : Filter.Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => 1 - (M * ((b - a) / N) / 4) ^ 2)
        Filter.atTop (nhds 1) := by simpa using Filter.Tendsto.const_sub 1 hg
    have h2 := h1.sqrt
    rw [Real.sqrt_one] at h2
    exact h2.const_mul θ
  have hfinal : θ * 1 ≤ fisherRaoLength p v a b / 2 := by
    refine le_of_tendsto hlim ?_
    filter_upwards [Filter.eventually_ge_atTop 1] with N hN using key N hN
  linarith

/-! ## The partition sums never exceed the length -/

/-- Every Bhattacharyya angle sum along an increasing chain of parameters is at
most the Fisher–Rao length of the corresponding piece of the curve. -/
theorem sum_two_arccos_bhattacharyya_le_fisherRaoLength {p v : ℝ → ι → ℝ}
    (hderiv : ∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun s => p s i) (v t i) t)
    (hv : ∀ i, Continuous fun t => v t i) (hpos : ∀ t i, 0 < p t i)
    (hp1 : ∀ t, ∑ i, p t i = 1) (T : ℕ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) (hmono : ∀ k < N, T k ≤ T (k + 1)) :
    ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, 2 * arccos (bhattacharyya (p (T k)) (p (T (k + 1))))
      ≤ fisherRaoLength p v (T 0) (T N) := by
  rw [← fisherRaoLength_sum_partition hderiv hv hpos T N]
  refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun k hk => ?_
  exact two_arccos_bhattacharyya_le_fisherRaoLength (hmono k (Finset.mem_range.mp hk))
    hderiv hv hpos hp1

/-! ## The reverse bound for fine partitions -/

/-- **One step of the lower bound.**  If the square-root velocity varies by at
most `e` on `[s,t]`, then the Euclidean chord between the endpoints of the
square-root curve is at least half the Fisher–Rao length minus `2 e (t−s)`. -/
theorem chord_ge_half_fisherRaoLength_sub {p v : ℝ → ι → ℝ}
    (hderiv : ∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun s => p s i) (v t i) t)
    (hv : ∀ i, Continuous fun t => v t i) (hpos : ∀ t i, 0 < p t i)
    {s t e : ℝ} (hst : s ≤ t) (he : 0 ≤ e)
    (hunif : ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc s t, ‖sqrtVelVec p v r - sqrtVelVec p v s‖ ≤ e) :
    (1 / 2) * fisherRaoLength p v s t - 2 * e * (t - s)
      ≤ √(∑ i, (√(p t i) - √(p s i)) ^ 2) := by
  set W : ℝ → ι → ℝ := sqrtVel p v with hW
  set n : ℝ := √(∑ i, (W s i) ^ 2) with hn
  have hn0 : 0 ≤ n := Real.sqrt_nonneg _
  have hnsq : n ^ 2 = ∑ i, (W s i) ^ 2 :=
    Real.sq_sqrt (Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => sq_nonneg _)
  have hnorm : ‖sqrtVelVec p v s‖ = n := norm_sqrtVelVec_eq_sqrt p v s
  -- the Fisher–Rao speed is bounded by `2 (n + e)` on `[s,t]`
  have hspeed : ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc s t, fisherRaoSpeed (p r) (v r) ≤ 2 * (n + e) := by
    intro r hr
    have h1 : ‖sqrtVelVec p v r‖ ≤ n + e := by
      have h2 : ‖sqrtVelVec p v r‖ ≤ ‖sqrtVelVec p v s‖ + ‖sqrtVelVec p v r - sqrtVelVec p v s‖ := by
        simpa using norm_le_norm_add_norm_sub' (sqrtVelVec p v r) (sqrtVelVec p v s)
      have h3 := hunif r hr
      rw [hnorm] at h2
      linarith
    rw [norm_sqrtVelVec hpos r] at h1
    linarith
  have hL : fisherRaoLength p v s t ≤ 2 * (n + e) * (t - s) :=
    fisherRaoLength_le_of_speed_le hderiv hv hpos hst hspeed
  -- the chord dominates `(n - e)(t - s)`
  have hchord : (n - e) * (t - s) ≤ √(∑ i, (√(p t i) - √(p s i)) ^ 2) := by
    rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hn0 with hn0' | hnpos
    · have : (n - e) * (t - s) ≤ 0 := by
        apply mul_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg <;> [linarith; linarith]
      exact this.trans (Real.sqrt_nonneg _)
    -- the unit test vector in the direction of the initial velocity
    set u : ι → ℝ := fun i => W s i / n with hu
    have husq : ∑ i, (u i) ^ 2 = 1 := by
      have : ∑ i, (u i) ^ 2 = (∑ i, (W s i) ^ 2) / n ^ 2 := by
        rw [Finset.sum_div]
        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by rw [hu]; field_simp
      rw [this, ← hnsq]
      field_simp
    -- Cauchy–Schwarz against the unit vector `u`
    have hCSgen : ∀ d : ι → ℝ, ∑ i, u i * d i ≤ √(∑ i, (d i) ^ 2) := by
      intro d
      have hCS := Finset.sum_mul_sq_le_sq_mul_sq Finset.univ u d
      rw [husq, one_mul] at hCS
      calc ∑ i, u i * d i ≤ |∑ i, u i * d i| := le_abs_self _
        _ = √((∑ i, u i * d i) ^ 2) := (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs _).symm
        _ ≤ √(∑ i, (d i) ^ 2) := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hCS
    -- the scalar test function and its derivative
    have hsqrtDeriv : ∀ r i, HasDerivAt (fun x => √(p x i)) (W r i) r :=
      fun r i => hasDerivAt_sqrt_coord (hderiv r i) (hpos r i)
    have hg : ∀ r : ℝ, HasDerivAt (fun x => ∑ i, u i * √(p x i)) (∑ i, u i * W r i) r :=
      fun r => HasDerivAt.fun_sum fun i _ => (hsqrtDeriv r i).const_mul (u i)
    have hgcont : Continuous fun r => ∑ i, u i * W r i :=
      continuous_finset_sum _ fun i _ =>
        continuous_const.mul (continuous_sqrtVel hderiv hv hpos i)
    have hFTC : (∫ r in s..t, ∑ i, u i * W r i)
        = (∑ i, u i * √(p t i)) - ∑ i, u i * √(p s i) :=
      integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt (fun r _ => hg r) (hgcont.intervalIntegrable s t)
    -- pointwise lower bound for the integrand
    have hpt : ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc s t, n - e ≤ ∑ i, u i * W r i := by
      intro r hr
      have hsplit : ∑ i, u i * W r i
          = (∑ i, u i * W s i) + ∑ i, u i * (W r i - W s i) := by
        rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring
      have hfirst : ∑ i, u i * W s i = n := by
        have : ∑ i, u i * W s i = (∑ i, (W s i) ^ 2) / n := by
          rw [Finset.sum_div]
          exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by rw [hu]; ring
        rw [this, ← hnsq]
        field_simp
      have hsecond : -e ≤ ∑ i, u i * (W r i - W s i) := by
        have hbd := hCSgen (fun i => W s i - W r i)
        have heq : √(∑ i, (W s i - W r i) ^ 2) ≤ e := by
          have h1 : ‖sqrtVelVec p v r - sqrtVelVec p v s‖
              = √(∑ i, (W r i - W s i) ^ 2) := norm_sqrtVelVec_sub r s
          have h2 : ∑ i, (W s i - W r i) ^ 2 = ∑ i, (W r i - W s i) ^ 2 :=
            Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring
          rw [h2, ← h1]
          exact hunif r hr
        have h3 : ∑ i, u i * (W s i - W r i) ≤ e := le_trans hbd heq
        have h4 : ∑ i, u i * (W s i - W r i) = -∑ i, u i * (W r i - W s i) := by
          rw [← Finset.sum_neg_distrib]
          exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring
        rw [h4] at h3
        linarith
      rw [hsplit, hfirst]
      linarith
    have hconst : IntervalIntegrable (fun _ : ℝ => n - e) volume s t :=
      _root_.intervalIntegrable_const
    have hint : (n - e) * (t - s) ≤ ∫ r in s..t, ∑ i, u i * W r i := by
      have h := intervalIntegral.integral_mono_on hst hconst (hgcont.intervalIntegrable s t) hpt
      rw [intervalIntegral.integral_const, smul_eq_mul, mul_comm (t - s) (n - e)] at h
      exact h
    -- Cauchy–Schwarz turns the increment of the test function into the chord
    have hdiff : (∑ i, u i * √(p t i)) - (∑ i, u i * √(p s i))
        ≤ √(∑ i, (√(p t i) - √(p s i)) ^ 2) := by
      have := hCSgen (fun i => √(p t i) - √(p s i))
      calc (∑ i, u i * √(p t i)) - (∑ i, u i * √(p s i))
          = ∑ i, u i * (√(p t i) - √(p s i)) := by
            rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
            exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by ring
        _ ≤ √(∑ i, (√(p t i) - √(p s i)) ^ 2) := this
    rw [hFTC] at hint
    linarith
  have hts : 0 ≤ t - s := by linarith
  nlinarith [hchord, hL, hts]

/-- **Reverse partition bound.**  For a partition whose steps are fine enough
that the square-root velocity varies by at most `e` on each of them, the
Bhattacharyya angle sum is within `4 e (b − a)` of the Fisher–Rao length. -/
theorem fisherRaoLength_le_sum_two_arccos_add {p v : ℝ → ι → ℝ}
    (hderiv : ∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun s => p s i) (v t i) t)
    (hv : ∀ i, Continuous fun t => v t i) (hpos : ∀ t i, 0 < p t i)
    (hp1 : ∀ t, ∑ i, p t i = 1) (T : ℕ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) (hmono : ∀ k < N, T k ≤ T (k + 1))
    {e : ℝ} (he : 0 ≤ e)
    (hunif : ∀ k < N, ∀ r ∈ Set.Icc (T k) (T (k + 1)),
      ‖sqrtVelVec p v r - sqrtVelVec p v (T k)‖ ≤ e) :
    fisherRaoLength p v (T 0) (T N)
      ≤ (∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, 2 * arccos (bhattacharyya (p (T k)) (p (T (k + 1)))))
        + 4 * e * (T N - T 0) := by
  have hstep : ∀ k ∈ Finset.range N, fisherRaoLength p v (T k) (T (k + 1))
      ≤ 2 * arccos (bhattacharyya (p (T k)) (p (T (k + 1)))) + 4 * e * (T (k + 1) - T k) := by
    intro k hk
    have hk' := Finset.mem_range.mp hk
    have hmk := hmono k hk'
    have hchord := chord_ge_half_fisherRaoLength_sub hderiv hv hpos hmk he (hunif k hk')
    have hangle : √(∑ i, (√(p (T (k + 1)) i) - √(p (T k) i)) ^ 2)
        ≤ arccos (bhattacharyya (p (T k)) (p (T (k + 1)))) := by
      have h := chord_le_arccos_bhattacharyya (p (T (k + 1))) (p (T k))
        (fun i => (hpos _ i).le) (fun i => (hpos _ i).le) (hp1 _) (hp1 _)
      rwa [bhattacharyya_comm] at h
    linarith
  calc fisherRaoLength p v (T 0) (T N)
      = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, fisherRaoLength p v (T k) (T (k + 1)) :=
        (fisherRaoLength_sum_partition hderiv hv hpos T N).symm
    _ ≤ ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N,
          (2 * arccos (bhattacharyya (p (T k)) (p (T (k + 1)))) + 4 * e * (T (k + 1) - T k)) :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum hstep
    _ = (∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, 2 * arccos (bhattacharyya (p (T k)) (p (T (k + 1)))))
          + 4 * e * (T N - T 0) := by
        rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
        congr 1
        rw [← Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_range_sub]

/-! ## The calibration theorem -/

/-- **Riemann convergence of the Bhattacharyya angle sums.**  For a `C¹` curve
of strictly positive probability vectors on `[a,b]`, the sums
`∑ₖ 2 arccos BC(p_{t_k}, p_{t_{k+1}})` converge to `fisherRaoLength p v a b` as
the mesh of the partition tends to `0`.  Hence the Fisher–Rao length functional
*is* the length structure induced by the Bhattacharyya angle metric. -/
theorem riemann_convergence_sum_two_arccos_bhattacharyya {p v : ℝ → ι → ℝ} {a b : ℝ}
    (hab : a ≤ b)
    (hderiv : ∀ t i, HasDerivAt (fun s => p s i) (v t i) t)
    (hv : ∀ i, Continuous fun t => v t i) (hpos : ∀ t i, 0 < p t i)
    (hp1 : ∀ t, ∑ i, p t i = 1) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ δ > 0, ∀ (N : ℕ) (T : ℕ → ℝ), T 0 = a → T N = b → (∀ k < N, T k ≤ T (k + 1)) →
      (∀ k < N, T (k + 1) - T k < δ) →
      |(∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, 2 * arccos (bhattacharyya (p (T k)) (p (T (k + 1)))))
        - fisherRaoLength p v a b| ≤ ε := by
  have hba : 0 ≤ b - a := by linarith
  have hden : (0:ℝ) < 4 * (b - a) + 1 := by linarith
  set e : ℝ := ε / (4 * (b - a) + 1) with hedef
  have he0 : 0 < e := div_pos hε hden
  -- uniform continuity of the square-root velocity on the compact interval
  have hunifc : UniformContinuousOn (sqrtVelVec p v) (Set.Icc a b) :=
    isCompact_Icc.uniformContinuousOn_of_continuous
      (continuous_sqrtVelVec hderiv hv hpos).continuousOn

# The Bhattacharyya angle as a spherical metric

This file develops the *spherical* side of the Fisher–Rao picture opened in
`Algebra.FisherRaoLength.Core`.  The square-root map

  `p ↦ (√p₁, …, √pₙ)`

of the images.  Consequently the *Bhattacharyya angle* `arccos BC(p,q)` is the
`InnerProductGeometry.angle` of the two images, i.e. the geodesic distance of
the round sphere.

## Main results

* `FisherRao.angle_sphereEmb` — `angle (√p) (√q) = arccos (BC p q)`
* `FisherRao.arccos_bhattacharyya_triangle` — the Bhattacharyya angle satisfies
  the triangle inequality (it is a genuine metric on the simplex)
* `FisherRao.arccos_bhattacharyya_le_sum` — its iterated (path) version
* `FisherRao.chord_eq_two_mul_sin_half_arccos` — the exact chord/angle relation

import Algebra.FisherRaoLength.Core

open Finset Real InnerProductGeometry

namespace FisherRao

variable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]

/-! ## The square-root embedding into Euclidean space -/

/-- The square-root embedding of a probability vector into `EuclideanSpace ℝ ι`.
For probability vectors it lands on the unit sphere. -/
noncomputable def sphereEmb (p : ι → ℝ) : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι := WithLp.toLp 2 fun i => √(p i)

omit [Fintype ι] in
@[simp] theorem sphereEmb_ofLp (p : ι → ℝ) (i : ι) : (sphereEmb p).ofLp i = √(p i) := rfl

/-- The Bhattacharyya coefficient is the Euclidean inner product of the
square-root embeddings. -/
theorem inner_sphereEmb (p q : ι → ℝ) (hp : ∀ i, 0 ≤ p i) :
    inner ℝ (sphereEmb p) (sphereEmb q) = bhattacharyya p q := by
  simp only [PiLp.inner_apply, RCLike.inner_apply, conj_trivial, sphereEmb_ofLp, bhattacharyya]
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => ?_
  rw [Real.sqrt_mul (hp i)]
  ring

/-- The square-root embedding of a probability vector is a unit vector. -/
theorem norm_sphereEmb (p : ι → ℝ) (hp : ∀ i, 0 ≤ p i) (hp1 : ∑ i, p i = 1) :
    ‖sphereEmb p‖ = 1 := by
  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_eq]
  have : ∀ i ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset ι), ‖(sphereEmb p).ofLp i‖ ^ 2 = p i := by
    intro i _
    rw [sphereEmb_ofLp, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs, Real.sq_sqrt (hp i)]
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl this, hp1, Real.sqrt_one]

/-- `BC (p, p) = 1` for a probability vector. -/
theorem bhattacharyya_self (p : ι → ℝ) (hp : ∀ i, 0 ≤ p i) (hp1 : ∑ i, p i = 1) :

  rw [bhattacharyya, ← hp1]
  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by
    rw [← sq, Real.sqrt_sq (hp i)]

/-- The Bhattacharyya coefficient is symmetric. -/
theorem bhattacharyya_comm (p q : ι → ℝ) : bhattacharyya p q = bhattacharyya q p :=
  Finset.sum_congr rfl fun i _ => by rw [mul_comm]

/-- `BC ≤ 1`: an instance of Cauchy–Schwarz on the sphere. -/
theorem bhattacharyya_le_one (p q : ι → ℝ) (hp : ∀ i, 0 ≤ p i) (hq : ∀ i, 0 ≤ q i)

  have h := sum_sub_sqrt_sq p q hp hq hp1 hq1

  linarith

/-- The Bhattacharyya angle is the spherical angle between the square-root
embeddings. -/
theorem angle_sphereEmb (p q : ι → ℝ) (hp : ∀ i, 0 ≤ p i) (hq : ∀ i, 0 ≤ q i)

    angle (sphereEmb p) (sphereEmb q) = arccos (bhattacharyya p q) := by
  have h : angle (sphereEmb p) (sphereEmb q)

  rw [h, inner_sphereEmb p q hp, norm_sphereEmb p hp hp1, norm_sphereEmb q hq hq1]
  norm_num

/-! ## The Bhattacharyya angle is a metric -/

/-- **Triangle inequality for the Bhattacharyya angle.**  The angle
`arccos BC` is the geodesic distance of the round sphere under the square-root
embedding, hence a metric on the simplex. -/
theorem arccos_bhattacharyya_triangle (p q r : ι → ℝ)

    (hp1 : ∑ i, p i = 1) (hq1 : ∑ i, q i = 1) (hr1 : ∑ i, r i = 1) :

  have h := angle_le_angle_add_angle (sphereEmb p) (sphereEmb q) (sphereEmb r)
  rwa [angle_sphereEmb p r hp hr hp1 hr1, angle_sphereEmb p q hp hq hp1 hq1,
    angle_sphereEmb q r hq hr hq1 hr1] at h

probability vectors the endpoint Bhattacharyya angle is at most the sum of the
consecutive angles. -/
theorem arccos_bhattacharyya_le_sum (P : ℕ → ι → ℝ)

      simp [bhattacharyya_self (P 0) (hp 0) (hp1 0)]

      have htri := arccos_bhattacharyya_triangle (P 0) (P n) (P (n + 1))

      linarith

  have hsum := sum_sub_sqrt_sq p q hp hq hp1 hq1
  rw [h] at hsum
  have hzero : ∀ i ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset ι), (√(p i) - √(q i)) ^ 2 = 0 := by

    rw [hsum, ← hcos, hdouble]; ring
  rw [this, Real.sqrt_sq (by positivity)]

  linarith

/-- On `[0, π/2]` one has `x cos x ≤ sin x` (the tangent inequality). -/
theorem mul_cos_le_sin_of_mem {x : ℝ} (hx0 : 0 ≤ x) (hx : x ≤ π / 2) :

  rcases eq_or_lt_of_le hx0 with h | hpos
  · simp [← h]

  · rw [h, Real.cos_pi_div_two, Real.sin_pi_div_two]; norm_num
  · have hc : 0 < cos x := Real.cos_pos_of_mem_Ioo ⟨by linarith [Real.pi_pos], hlt⟩

    rw [Real.tan_eq_sin_div_cos, lt_div_iff₀ hc] at h

    Real.sin_nonneg_of_nonneg_of_le_pi hx0 (by linarith [Real.pi_pos])
  have hcos0 : 0 ≤ cos x := Real.cos_nonneg_of_mem_Icc ⟨by linarith [Real.pi_pos], hxπ⟩

    have hle : 1 - s ^ 2 ≤ cos x ^ 2 := by nlinarith
    calc √(1 - s ^ 2) ≤ √(cos x ^ 2) := Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hle
      _ = cos x := Real.sqrt_sq hcos0

  have hsin : sin (arccos (bhattacharyya p q) / 2) ≤ m / 2 := by
    have h := (chord_eq_two_mul_sin_half_arccos p q hp hq hp1 hq1) ▸ hchord
    linarith
  have := angle_mul_sqrt_le_of_sin_half_le (Real.arccos_nonneg (bhattacharyya p q))
    (Real.arccos_le_pi _) (by linarith) hsin
  linarith
